text: The case state change and the creation item of the timeline are read as the decision records of the case, in time order, from the decision-record query of rwb-decision; rwb-case adds no status-history table and keeps no second copy of the history, and the creation of a case is its first decision record, which carries the entry rule and its version.
why: The legacy story read its own module's decision_log_entry and showed a status-change item and a creation item, but no P3 table holds a case status history and the decision record now lives with P7, so the story and the contract need one stated source.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 4, 11 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (assignment and recovery_case); context pack P3 ownership rows (15 tables); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03
confirm: Solution architect with the P7 owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1035-CON.
impact: If P7 brings its own case-event query or a status history is added later, one consumed row, the DecisionRecordClient mapping and two mocks change; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: A transfer item takes its to queue from assignment.queue_id (DF-WRK-039) and its reason code from assignment.transfer_reason_code (DF-WRK-040), and its from queue and from owner from the closed previous assignment row of the same case (ended_at set), with the queue codes resolved on the queue table of rwb_case; the rule ID comes from assignment.rule_id (DF-WRK-016) and the rule version from the decision record of the transfer, never from a column.
why: AC2 and the legacy section 12 show the from and to queue and owner plus the rule version of a transfer, but assignment has no from-queue column and no rule-version column, so the detail needs a stated derivation that invents no field.
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 assignment DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-040; legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 11 and 12; legacy RWB-E1-021 transfer with reason; context pack P3 tables (assignment, queue)
confirm: Solution architect with the P3 owner and the P7 owner at the baseline review, before TC-E1-035-02 is signed off.
impact: A dedicated from-queue column later is one additive column and one mapper line; the item shape and the AC are unchanged.

text: REQ-WKM-003 and REQ-ACA-005 are traced through their business rules and test cases only: the legacy trace table gives a BRD section for REQ-CWC-016 and REQ-OCC-007 alone, so the two other requirement rows carry the placeholder and no section is invented.
why: The story cites four requirement IDs but the legacy trace table maps two of them to a BRD section, and the target files must not invent a section number.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-035 section 18; section 8 BR3 and BR5; metadata row BRD section (Epic 1, 3.3 and 3.6; Program, 5.3 and 5.6)
confirm: Business analyst with the BRD owner when the Epic 1 BRD next version is reviewed.
impact: Two cells of one trace table change when the sections are published; no criterion, table or contract changes.

text: The decision-record query of rwb-decision is one GET operation keyed by case, with an optional from and to filter, returning the decision code, rule ID, rule version, approver, final call and decision time of each record, with caseId as the key, one hop, a 2 s timeout and a GET retry once with jitter; the exact path is taken from C RWB-P7-E1027-CON when it is published.
why: The timeline cannot compose, mock or test the decision items without a read operation, and no source gives the path, the filter or the field list of the query that replaces the legacy DecisionLogQuery interface.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-035 section 12 (DecisionLogQuery.entriesForCase, DecisionLogSummary); section 11 DF-DEC-002 to DF-DEC-016; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03 and DP-11; Architecture v5 shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1
confirm: P7 decision owner in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1035-CON.
impact: A different path or field list changes one consumed row, the DecisionRecordClient adapter and one fake; the item schema is unaffected because the mapper reads by field name.

text: RWB-P3-E1035-CON publishes version v1.1 of the timeline operation as an additive minor version inside major version 1 of the document of RWB-P3-E1023-CON: the path, the five query parameters and the error envelope are unchanged, the item gains reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode, ruleId and actorType, and the page gains the total and one section entry per source.
why: Two contract stories of the same service describe the same operation and no source says which owns which field or how the addition is versioned, so a default is needed before the panel and the edge can build.
read: RWB-P3-E1023-CON sections 11 and 12.1; legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 12 and 15; Template and Rules R8.2 and R7.2 s12; ADR-020
confirm: Solution architect with the gateway-bff owner before the additive check is made the merge gate.
impact: If the baseline is re-cut instead, one version number, one checksum and the compatibility baseline change; the item fields and the ACs do not.

text: The Case record R check and the scope filter come from the authorise guard of the rwb-case service template, already wired by RWB-P3-E1023-APP, so this story adds no access decoupling row and no new contract dependency; AC7 and the access test prove it through the rwb-access contract mock.
why: The WP pattern list for this key names ten patterns and none is the access guard, while the legacy story still needs the scope and the right, so the guard has to be named as inherited instead of re-decoupled.
read: RWB-P3-E1023-APP sections 1, 3 and 12.2; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-08 and R5.4 class C; legacy RWB-E1-035 sections 3, 5 and 10
confirm: Solution architect with the P4 access owner at the wave 1 baseline review.
impact: If the guard lands later than RWB-P3-E1023-APP, AC7 waits on it; no field, table or event changes.

text: The legacy story RWB-E1-035 carries the status Ready for build while no approval of its BRD, PRD or backlog entry is recorded in the workspace, and no approval is required to proceed in this run, so both target stories are written and released as Draft (realignment v1) and the release date 30 November 2026 is copied unchanged as tentative.
why: The D-RCV-60 overlay settles a missing approval or status as an assumption, and the realignment cannot wait for one.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-035 metadata rows Status and Epic; Template and Rules R1 U2, U7 and R8.1; root AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
applied_in: RWB-P3-E1035-APP metadata and change log; RWB-P3-E1035-CON metadata and change log
confirm: Programme delivery lead at the stage gate of wave 1.
impact: A recorded approval changes the Status row and the tracker entry only; no content changes.
